extraction.summary: This paper fits Wess-Zumino dark radiation (WZDR) and new atomic dark matter (nuADaM) with ACT DR6 small-scale CMB spectra plus Planck, CMB lensing, BAO, supernovae, and optional S8/SH0ES information. The authors find that the high-ell damping-tail data restrict extra radiation in both transition models: without SH0ES, their quoted 95% upper bounds are N_IR<0.246 (WZDR) and N_idr<0.237 (nuADaM), while fits including SH0ES reach H0 around 70 km/s/Mpc with a worse CMB fit. A separate free-streaming plus perfect-fluid radiation extension finds no preference for a self-interacting component. These are model- and likelihood-conditioned fits; they do not test Hot NEDE or a running primordial spectrum directly.

ideas.title: WZDR scalar threshold transfers entropy to a self-interacting fermion bath
ideas.description: The proposed dark sector contains a massive complex scalar and a massless Weyl fermion with a Yukawa interaction. The paper assumes the dark sector is populated after BBN, scalar decays remain in equilibrium, and fermion self-interactions keep chemical and kinetic equilibrium through recombination. When Td falls below m_phi, the scalar becomes nonrelativistic and its entropy heats the remaining fermions over roughly a decade in redshift. The text says the effective relativistic count rises from N_UV to N_IR=(15/7)^(1/3)N_UV. The fitted parameters are late radiation density and a transition location; the fixed ratio is the complex-scalar/Weyl-fermion degree-of-freedom prediction.
locators: Sec. 2.1, PDF p.3, paragraph after Eq. (2.1); HTML #S2.SS1.p1.2

equations.domain: Dark-sector description; early relativistic regime Td >> m_phi and transition as Td falls through m_phi.

ideas.title: nuADaM couples a dark-radiation fluid to an atomic dark-matter subcomponent until dark recombination
ideas.description: A subcomponent of dark matter consists of oppositely charged dark protons and electrons under a dark U(1). Dark photons mix kinetically with a massless vector X and charged massless fermions, keeping the radiation self-interacting. At high temperatures the charged matter is ionized and scatters from dark radiation; below the dark binding scale it recombines and decouples. The paper describes effective parameters N_idr, the atomic-dark-matter fraction f_idm, and transition scale factor a_t; it fixes alpha_d=0.01 and m_p'=1 GeV and uses m_e'/m_p' to control the transition. The fit section instead varies r_twin without defining it in the paper text.
locators: Sec. 2.2, PDF p.4, parameter paragraph; HTML #S2.SS2

equations.locator: PDF Eq. (2.2), p.4; HTML #S2.E2 (equation-group rows #S2.E2X/#S2.E2Y); PDF render visually checked.
equations.definitions: F' is the dark-photon field strength; X is the second dark vector field strength; p' and e' are dark proton/electron; nu'_j are charged massless fermions; epsilon is the kinetic mixing; D is the dark covariant derivative; N_f counts the dark fermion species.
equations.domain: The paper’s cosmological regime with dark radiation self-interacting through the stated kinetic mixing and dark recombination before matter-radiation equality.

equations.definitions: T is the relevant dark-sector temperature; alpha_d is the dark fine-structure constant; m_e' is the dark-electron mass.
equations.domain: Asymptotic temperature regimes; the paper does not present this as a sharp, exact recombination condition.

ideas.title: ACT DR6 damping-tail data sharply reduce allowed radiation in the fitted WZDR and nuADaM models
ideas.description: For P-ACT-LBS without SH0ES, the authors report 95% limits N_IR<0.246 for WZDR and N_idr<0.237 for nuADaM, with H0 means 68.75 and 68.64 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 respectively. With SH0ES, they report H0 around 70.13 (WZDR) and 70.48 (nuADaM), but describe a degraded CMB fit; the Table 1 best fits remain over 2 sigma below the SH0ES central value. Restricting ACT to ell<3000 gives similar 95% upper bounds, 0.266 and 0.256. These are posterior summaries under the paper’s dataset and parameter choices, not direct measurements of H0 or universal bounds on dark radiation.
locators: Sec. 4, PDF pp.5-10, Fig.2, Fig.3, Fig.4, Tables 1-3; HTML #S4

ideas.title: The reported WZDR and nuADaM limits are stable when ACT multipoles above 3000 are removed
ideas.description: The fits with ell_max=3000 yield only slightly weaker quoted radiation bounds than the ell_max=6500 fits. The authors infer that the constraining power is mainly in the intermediate damping tail, 1000<ell<3000, where they argue Silk damping is measurable and secondary anisotropies are less dominant. This tests the sensitivity to removing high multipoles in their adopted ACT likelihood; it does not vary the foreground model or demonstrate absence of model-dependent likelihood bias.
locators: Sec. 4, PDF pp.7-9, Fig.4, Tables 2-3; HTML #S4

equations.domain: Authors’ interpretation of the ell_max cut comparison.

ideas.title: ACT DR6 finds no preference for partitioning radiation into free-streaming and perfect-fluid components
ideas.description: The authors add independently variable free-streaming radiation N_fs and a self-interacting perfect relativistic fluid with w=c_s^2=1/3, define N_tot=N_fs+N_idr, and report N_tot=2.87±0.13 at 68% CL, N_idr<0.187, and no preference for nonzero interacting radiation. They say this agrees with the ACT DR6 baseline Neff=2.86±0.13. This is a deliberately limited two-component phenomenology, not a test of arbitrary interacting-radiation perturbation closures.
locators: Sec. 4, PDF pp.7-10, Figure 5; HTML #S4.F5 and surrounding text

equations.locator: Sec. 4, PDF pp.7-8 and Figure 5, p.9; HTML #S4.
equations.definitions: N_fs denotes the free-streaming component (including SM neutrinos as described); N_idr denotes additional self-interacting radiation.
equations.domain: Generalized analysis with a tightly coupled perfect-fluid radiation component.

author_proposals_and_model_assumptions: WZDR entropy transfer across a scalar mass threshold, with dark sector populated after BBN and self-interactions in equilibrium through recombination.
nuADaM dark atom formation/decoupling near equality with a self-interacting radiation fluid.
Generalized additional radiation as a free-streaming plus perfect-fluid split with w=c_s^2=1/3.
author_fitted_results: ACT+Planck+low-redshift data restrict N_IR and N_idr in the two fitted models; quoted 95% bounds are <0.246 and <0.237 without SH0ES.
The SH0ES-conditioned fit moves H0 upward to about 70 km/s/Mpc but worsens the CMB chi-square; Table 1 best-fit H0 values are 70.04 (WZDR) and 70.63 (nuADaM), versus 68.71 for LCDM.
The generalized fit reports N_tot=2.87±0.13 (68% CL) and no preference for N_idr>0.
author_interpretations: Extra radiation increases Silk damping and is disfavored by ACT high-ell spectra in the fitted models.
Similar constraints after ell_max=3000 suggest intermediate multipoles 1000<ell<3000 carry much of the constraining power.
The paper concludes these transitions do not preserve the earlier Planck-only H0-relieving parameter space, but explicitly leaves open other radiation-sector mechanisms.
reader_inferences: Methods and tables have nomenclature drift: WZDR is described using N_IR but Table 1 labels the row ΔN_idr; the transition is log10(z_t) in Sec.2.1 and log10(a_t) in Methods/Tables. nuADaM lists f_idm in its model description but varies r_twin without a definition in the prose.

The generalized-model paragraph says DESI DR1 is used; the precise BAO release for the adjacent WZDR/nuADaM Tables 2-3 is not explicitly restated, so avoid silently assigning DR1 or DR2 to those rows.

Table 1 total chi-square values do not equal the sum of the separately listed CMB, BAO, SN, and M_B components. The methods also include KiDS S8 but the table has no chi-square_S8 row; the source does not specify the missing term or any additive normalization convention. The table-to-total accounting therefore cannot be reconstructed from the paper alone; this is not enough to claim a calculation error.

extraction.strongest_objection: The broadest conclusion is more general than the fitted physics: the paper constrains two specific transition models and one restricted free-streaming plus perfect-fluid split, under the adopted ACT/Planck/BAO/SN likelihood and baseline assumptions. It does not establish a bound on arbitrary interacting-radiation perturbations, Hot NEDE’s distinct background/matter-decoupling history, or compensating primordial-spectrum running. The source also leaves parameter and table-conditioning details (notably r_twin, a_t versus z_t, and the BAO release scope) insufficiently explicit for a clean independent reproduction.
extraction.most_informative_next_test: First complete the already queued source reading of arxiv:2604.26541v1 as a separate paper. For a later quantitative comparison, hold the ACT DR6 likelihood and shared nuisance/foreground setup fixed and compare the same WZDR or nuADaM branch with a power-law primordial spectrum versus a clearly defined running extension, reporting posterior predictive TT/TE/EE residuals over 1000<ell<3000 and exact likelihood/code/prior identities. Keep Hot NEDE as a separate model branch with its own closure; do not transfer these bounds or combine mechanisms before their contracts are checked. No such test was run here.

usefulness.assessment: Useful constraint-context reading for interacting dark radiation and an informative boundary against overgeneralizing ACT DR6 results. It is not evidence against Hot NEDE and does not settle the running-versus-radiation degeneracy.
usefulness.readiness: full Luna reading packet prepared; Sol scientific review remains required before idea/graph acceptance or design promotion.
usefulness.strongest_supported_conclusion: Under this paper’s WZDR and nuADaM model parameterizations and stated combined datasets, ACT DR6 substantially lowers the allowed additional radiation and SH0ES-conditioned H0 remains around 70 rather than the SH0ES central value.

caveats: The abstract says WZDR induces a step-like reduction in dark-radiation abundance, while Sec.2.1 describes the effective radiation count increasing from N_UV to N_IR as scalar entropy heats the fermions. This may refer to different abundance variables; the distinction should be clarified rather than treating the wording as a contradiction or equating the quantities.
The exact fitted interpretation of nuADaM r_twin is not defined in this paper; no meaning should be guessed from f_idm or source-code conventions.
Posterior limits, best fits, means, and confidence levels are source-conditioned fits, not direct measurements or independent reproductions.
The restriction ell_max=3000 is a likelihood-range sensitivity check within the adopted analysis, not a re-evaluation of ACT foreground/calibration modeling for non-LCDM spectra.
The source cites registered papers at author-year anchors whose HTML anchor numbers differ from the printed PDF bibliography labels. Both locators are retained in citation_links.

Table 1 reports S8 but omits a chi-square_S8 contribution, and its listed component chi-squares do not sum to chi-square total. The missing term and any normalization convention are not explained; do not diagnose a calculation error from the table alone.
